## COMPANY OVERVIEW

Two Bit Digital Ltd is a SaaS development and AI engineering studio incorporated in England and Wales (Companies House No. 14710072). The company builds mission-critical digital systems for enterprises, government bodies, and regulated markets across the United Kingdom, United States, Australia, and Pakistan.

The studio is founded and led by Muhammad Wasif (Founder & CEO). Muhammad has deep experience in software architecture, product engineering, and building for regulated industries. He led the development of Tikkit X — a cryptographically secure offline event ticketing platform — and is the principal architect of Terra Core, a zero-knowledge document intelligence engine.

### Cryptographic Audit Trail System (FCA Examination)

Sector: Compliance & RegTech | Region: United Kingdom | Duration: 6 weeks

Challenge: A regulated professional services firm faced FCA examination requiring a complete, tamper-evident audit trail. Existing system had only database timestamps.

Solution: Cryptographically chained audit log — each event hash includes the previous event hash. Back-filled 3 years of historical data. Regulatory disclosure export tool built in.

Outcomes: 2.3M audit events chained and verified, no FCA examination findings, disclosure pack time reduced from 4 hours to 12 minutes.

## INSIGHTS ARTICLES

### AI Workflows Explained: How Businesses Are Automating Operations in 2025

Published: 2026-04-27 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/what-are-ai-workflows

An AI workflow is a sequence of automated steps in which one or more AI models process, analyse, or generate content as part of a broader business process. Unlike traditional rule-based automation, AI workflows handle unstructured inputs — documents, emails, images, and natural language — and produce structured outputs that feed into systems and decisions.

The six main types of AI workflows: document processing (extract, classify, summarise from unstructured documents), decision routing (classify and route incoming requests), conversational agents (natural language task completion), data transformation (structure unstructured datasets), compliance monitoring (continuously check against regulatory rules), and content generation (draft reports, summaries, correspondence at scale).

AI workflows differ from traditional automation in their ability to handle variability — an LLM-based document processor reads invoices in any format by understanding semantic meaning, not character position. Building an AI workflow requires six stages: map the current process, identify AI-suitable steps, choose the right architecture (prompt engineering vs RAG vs agent frameworks), build with human oversight from day one, connect to existing systems, and monitor continuously.

Two Bit Digital builds AI workflows for legal, financial, and enterprise sectors using Anthropic Claude and OpenAI APIs, RAG architectures on Supabase pgvector, and Next.js orchestration layers.

### Custom Software vs. Off-the-Shelf: Why Bespoke Solutions Win for Growing Businesses

Published: 2026-04-24 | Category: SaaS Development
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/custom-software-vs-off-the-shelf

The decision between custom and off-the-shelf software is not primarily about cost — it is about fit, scalability, and competitive differentiation. Off-the-shelf software trades fit for speed; custom software trades speed for fit. Off-the-shelf makes sense when processes are generic and not a source of competitive advantage. Custom software is necessary when a core process is genuinely differentiating, when regulatory requirements exceed what standard tools can accommodate, when integration requirements are complex, or when the product itself is what is being sold.

The correct cost comparison is not build cost versus subscription cost but total five-year cost of ownership: build cost plus maintenance versus subscription plus implementation plus customisation plus workaround labour plus switching costs. Two Bit Digital delivers custom software with full IP ownership transferred to the client on final payment.

---

### How to Build an AI Automation Strategy for Your Business

Published: 2026-04-21 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/how-to-build-an-ai-automation-strategy

A coherent AI automation strategy follows six steps: audit current processes (map every repeating process, its inputs, outputs, and decision points), identify automation candidates (score by volume, complexity, and strategic value), choose the right AI approach (prompt engineering for classification tasks, RAG for knowledge-intensive tasks, agent frameworks for multi-step autonomous work, traditional automation for fully deterministic processes), decide whether to build or partner (if AI is your core product build internally; if AI is a capability layer, partnering is usually the better economic decision), start with one workflow not ten, and measure and expand.

The failure mode for AI strategies is trying to automate everything simultaneously. A well-built, well-monitored single workflow that saves ten hours per week is more valuable than ten half-built experiments that each save one.

---

### What Is a RAG System? How AI Can Search and Learn From Your Own Documents

Published: 2026-04-17 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/what-is-a-rag-system

RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is an AI architecture that combines a retrieval system searching a document collection with a generation model that uses retrieved content to produce grounded responses. Documents are split into chunks, converted into numerical embeddings capturing semantic meaning, and stored in a vector database. When a question is asked, it is embedded and matched against document chunks with similar semantic content. The most relevant chunks are passed to the LLM alongside the question, and the model generates a response grounded in those specific documents.

RAG is superior to standard LLMs for business because responses are grounded in actual documents (not potentially outdated training data), outputs are citable (the system identifies which documents informed each response), the knowledge base is updatable without retraining, hallucination is reduced by constraining the model to retrieved content, and auditability meets regulated industry compliance requirements. Best use cases: legal document Q&A, internal knowledge bases, customer support, compliance checking, and due diligence.

Two Bit Digital builds RAG systems using OpenAI embeddings and Supabase pgvector. Terra Core is built on this architecture.

---

### The Hidden Cost of Manual Business Processes

Published: 2026-04-14 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/hidden-cost-of-manual-business-processes

Manual processes cost more than the salary of the person performing them. McKinsey research finds that approximately 60% of all occupations have at least 30% of activities automatable with current technology. Hidden costs beyond salary include: error remediation (manual data entry has a 1-4% error rate with significant downstream remediation costs), process latency (waiting time at every handover limits throughput), opportunity cost (skilled staff performing repetitive tasks instead of differentiating work), compliance risk (inconsistent manual execution creates audit exposure), and staff retention cost (capable employees performing repetitive work are more likely to leave, with recruitment costs often exceeding £15,000 per hire).

A straightforward ROI calculation: hours saved per week multiplied by hourly fully-loaded cost multiplied by 52, minus annualised automation cost. A process consuming ten hours per week of a £25/hour role represents £13,000 per year in direct labour saving.

### Event Management Software in 2025: What Every Organiser Needs

Published: 2026-04-09 | Category: Event Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/event-management-software-guide-2025

Event management software handles the full lifecycle of running an event: registration, ticketing, guest management, payments, check-in, and analytics. Essential features include event creation and publishing, RSVP and registration management, unique verifiable QR codes per attendee, mobile check-in scanning from any device, payment processing through local payment methods, real-time analytics, staff scanner access without account creation, offline check-in capability, and post-event reporting.

The most important feature most platforms get wrong is offline capability. A QR check-in system requiring a live server connection fails in venues with unreliable internet — at exactly the moment it matters most. The correct architecture is offline-first: cryptographically signed tickets that verify on-device without a server round-trip. Tikkit X implements HMAC-SHA256 offline QR verification and supports JazzCash, EasyPaisa, and bank transfer for the Pakistani market.

---

### How Offline QR Verification Is Solving Event Fraud Without the Internet

Published: 2026-04-07 | Category: Event Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/offline-qr-verification-event-ticketing

Standard QR check-in systems encode a ticket ID in the QR code and send it to a server for validation at scan time — requiring a live internet connection for every scan. Under load (hundreds of simultaneous arrivals in a venue with saturated bandwidth), these systems slow down, time out, or fail.

Offline QR verification embeds a cryptographic signature in the QR code at issuance. The HMAC-SHA256 signing process: the server generates a payload (ticket ID, event ID, attendee identifier, timestamp) and signs it with a secret key using HMAC-SHA256. The payload and signature are encoded into the QR. At scan time, the device recomputes the signature using its pre-loaded key copy — if it matches, the ticket is valid. No network call required. Duplicate scan detection runs in local device state, syncing to the server when connectivity is restored.

HMAC-SHA256 signatures cannot be forged without the secret key, making ticket fabrication computationally infeasible. Tikkit X implements this architecture for all tickets.

### From Guest List to Gate: A Complete Guide to Running a Paperless Event

Published: 2026-03-24 | Category: Event Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/how-to-run-a-paperless-event-pakistan

Six steps to a fully digital event: (1) Set up the event on Tikkit X — name, date, capacity, ticket types, registration mode (open or invite-only) in under two minutes. (2) Configure the registration form — guest details, CNIC where required, category or gender ratio limits. (3) Share the registration link — guests register on any device, pay through JazzCash, EasyPaisa, or bank transfer, and receive a unique QR code immediately. (4) Monitor registrations in real time — approve or decline pending registrations, manage the waitlist, message all registered guests from the dashboard. (5) Run check-in on the day — open the scanner on any mobile device, share a scanner link with door staff (no accounts needed), scan QRs instantly with or without internet. (6) Review post-event analytics — total registrations, check-in rate, arrival timeline, revenue, and individual guest records with timestamps.

Common mistakes: not testing scanner setup before doors open, using a single device for large events, not briefing door staff on the flow, not confirming offline mode works before the event.

### Digital Transformation for Law Firms: The Complete Guide

Published: 2026-03-17 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/law-firm-digital-transformation-guide

Law firm digital transformation means replacing the fragmented combination of manual processes, paper files, and disconnected tools with a coherent digital system covering both client-facing and internal operations. Why most firms still run on paper and email: workflows were established before modern SaaS existed, legal software has historically been expensive and poorly designed for smaller practices, senior fee earners resist time investment in transition, and compliance requirements create risk aversion.

The client-facing digital layer includes: a professional SEO-optimised website, online consultation booking, a client portal (authenticated access to case status, case diary, and shared documents), a lawyer case diary visible to clients, secure document access, and a judgements library where applicable. The internal management layer includes: matter management, procedural deadline tracking, document management, case file digitisation, employee and role management, billing and time recording, and audit trail logging.

YKC Legal (ykclegal.org), built by Two Bit Digital, demonstrates the client-facing layer. Averon Legal Systems provides the internal management platform. Timeline: 4–6 weeks for client-facing layer, 8–12 weeks for internal platform, 3–6 months for full paper file digitisation.

### CPR Part 47 Compliance Software: What UK Costs Lawyers Need

Published: 2026-03-10 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/cpr-part-47-compliance-software

CPR Part 47 governs detailed assessment of costs in English and Welsh civil litigation — setting specific, non-negotiable timelines for serving the bill of costs, filing the notice of commencement, responding to points of dispute, and requesting hearings. Missing these deadlines carries consequences ranging from cost sanctions to loss of right to assessment.

Operational challenges: multiple interdependent deadlines per matter (each stage triggers the next), high matter volume (costs professionals manage dozens of simultaneous matters), variable trigger events (some deadlines run from service, some from filing, some from court orders), Part 36 offer monitoring requiring simultaneous tracking alongside Part 47 timelines, and document management across bills, points of dispute, replies, and supporting documents.

What CPR Part 47 compliance software must do: model CPR procedural stages explicitly with automatic deadline calculation from trigger events; configurable automated alerts at defined intervals; Part 36 offer tracking integrated with Part 47 timelines; role-based dashboards for partners, supervisors, and fee earners; structured CPR-specific document management with client portal access; tamper-evident audit trail; and database-level multi-tenant isolation.

Averon Legal Systems — built by Two Bit Digital — is a purpose-built CPR Part 47 and Part 36 platform currently in beta for UK costs practices.

---

### Why Your Law Firm Needs a Client Portal

Published: 2026-03-03 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/law-firm-client-portal-guide

The most common complaint clients have about their lawyers is not the legal advice — it is the communication. A law firm client portal is a secure, authenticated web interface where clients access information about their matter. A complete portal includes: case status dashboard, lawyer case diary (chronological record of all significant matter events), document access (secure access to client-visible documents), hearing and deadline calendar, team information, consultation booking, and secure messaging.

A case diary answers the question clients most commonly want answered: what has actually happened in my case? It removes the need for update calls, demonstrates active matter progression, and builds client confidence. Security requirements: HTTPS, password authentication, session management, matter-level access controls ensuring each client sees only their own data, and audit logging of all access events.

Business benefits for the firm: reduced inbound calls from clients chasing updates, higher client satisfaction and referral rates, professional differentiation, reduced onboarding friction, and documented communication records. YKC Legal (ykclegal.org) provides a live example built by Two Bit Digital.

### Case File Digitisation for Law Firms

Published: 2026-02-24 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/law-firm-case-file-digitisation

Seven-step law firm digitisation process: (1) Audit paper volume — count active and archived matters, estimate volume, identify files eligible for destruction under retention policy. (2) Prioritise active cases — digitise currently active matters first for immediate operational benefit. (3) Establish scanning and OCR workflow — use a dedicated document scanner (50+ pages per minute) and scan to searchable PDF using OCR. (4) Define naming convention and folder taxonomy before scanning begins — naming must encode matter reference, document type, date, and version consistently. (5) Implement role-based access controls at system level — fee earners see assigned matters only, with all access logged. (6) Plan the physical archive — maintain originals for active matters until conclusion, follow retention policy for archives, use certified confidential waste for destruction. (7) Train the team and enforce the standards.

Most common mistakes: starting with archives rather than active matters; scanning without OCR (image-only PDFs cannot be searched); building folder structure during scanning rather than before; no written naming convention; insufficient access controls; no backup and disaster recovery plan.

---

### Law Firm Employee Management Software

Published: 2026-02-17 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/law-firm-employee-management-software

Generic HR software does not address the specific requirements of legal practice management. Fee earners bill time against specific matters. Supervisors need team workload visibility without accessing every file's full detail. Partners need portfolio-level performance data. Document access must be controlled at matter level. None of these requirements are satisfied by standard tools.

Law firm employee management software must be matter-centric: time, tasks, and documents all attached to the matter as the organising unit. Role-based dashboards: fee earners see their own matters, deadlines, and time recording; supervisors see team workload distribution and deadline risk; partners see portfolio-level billing performance and team utilisation. Time recording must link every unit of time to a specific matter and task type, feeding directly into billing. Access controls must be enforced at database level — not just by application convention.

Averon Legal Systems implements role-based dashboards, matter-linked time recording, task allocation with workload visibility, and database-level document access controls for UK costs practices.

### End-to-End Legal Tech: How One Platform Can Run Your Entire Law Firm

Published: 2026-02-10 | Category: Legal Technology
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/end-to-end-legal-tech-platform

The typical law firm technology stack is not a stack but a collection: a case management system that does not talk to the document store, a client portal not connected to the matter system, a time recording tool requiring manual export for billing. Staff spend 20–30% of their day moving information between disconnected systems.

A complete law firm digital stack includes: professional website, client portal, matter management, document management, procedural deadline engine, employee management, billing and time recording, client intake workflow, and audit trail. Integration delivers the highest value: when a fee earner updates the case diary internally, it appears in the client portal immediately; when a document is filed and marked client-visible, it appears in their document access view automatically.

Risks of fragmented approach: data inconsistency (same information maintained separately in multiple systems eventually diverges), compliance gaps (audit trails that stop at system boundaries), integration technical debt (connecting disparate systems after the fact is expensive and fragile), complex staff training, and vendor dependency risk.

Two Bit Digital delivers the complete stack: YKC Legal demonstrates the client-facing layer; Averon Legal Systems provides the internal management platform.

### What Is a SaaS Development Studio?

Published: 2026-02-03 | Category: SaaS Development
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/what-is-a-saas-development-studio

A SaaS development studio is a specialist engineering firm that designs and builds Software-as-a-Service products. The defining characteristic is orientation toward product: multi-tenant architecture, scalable data models, billing infrastructure, role-based access control, API design, and operational requirements of software running reliably at scale for paying customers.

How a SaaS studio differs from a digital agency: agencies are oriented toward marketing, brand, and communications; studios toward engineering and product. Agencies deliver websites and campaigns; studios deliver working software users interact with daily. Studios design for scale, security, and maintainability from the first line of code. Studios operate their own products — the most reliable signal that their engineers understand production software requirements.

How a SaaS studio differs from a freelance team: a studio has legal accountability, professional indemnity insurance, defined processes, and team continuity even as individuals change. For software operating over years, these structural factors matter as much as individual engineering capability.

When you need a SaaS studio: building multi-tenant software, serving regulated markets, needing AI integrated as a core feature, recovering from a failed agency build, or needing a long-term technical partner.

Two Bit Digital is a SaaS development studio (Companies House 14710072) that owns and operates Tikkit X (live), Averon Legal Systems (beta), and Terra Core (in development).

---

### From Idea to Product: Inside Two Bit Digital's AI Engineering Process

Published: 2026-01-27 | Category: SaaS Development
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/inside-two-bit-digital-ai-engineering-process

Five-phase process used on every Two Bit Digital build: (1) Discovery and architecture design — map user types, workflows, data, and regulatory constraints; design data model, permission structure, and API architecture before writing code. (2) Engineering foundation — database schema and row-level security, authentication, RBAC, multi-tenant isolation, deployment pipeline. (3) AI and integration layer — LLM API integration, RAG pipeline (embedding, vector storage, retrieval), prompt engineering and versioning, confidence thresholds and human oversight logic, audit logging for every AI interaction, and connections to external systems. (4) Quality assurance and compliance review — functional testing plus compliance review: does the audit trail capture every required event? Do access controls correctly enforce permissions? Do failure modes (API unavailable, low-confidence output, malformed input) behave correctly? (5) Deployment and ongoing support — staging environment review, smoke tests, monitoring and alerting, incident response procedures, then ongoing feature development and scaling support.

Tikkit X went from concept to production in under four months through this process. Averon Legal Systems went from discovery to beta in six months, including full compliance review against SRA requirements and GDPR obligations.

### How We Built a CPR-Compliant Legal SaaS in Six Months: The Averon Story

Published: 2026-01-20 | Category: SaaS Development
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/building-averon-legal-systems-case-study

Averon Legal Systems was built to replace spreadsheet-based CPR Part 47 and Part 36 matter tracking for UK costs lawyers. Compliance constraints mapped before any code was written: CPR required explicit modelling of procedural stages with variable trigger-based timelines; SRA required matter-level access control isolation; GDPR required data processing agreements with all third-party services and a Data Protection Impact Assessment.

Core architecture decision: Supabase (PostgreSQL) with row-level security policies enforcing access control at the database level — so even an application bug cannot allow cross-tenant data access. The multi-tenant security model was built and tested independently before any user-facing features were developed.

The CPR deadline engine models each Part 47 procedural stage as a state, with transitions triggered by user actions (serving the bill, filing the notice of commencement, receiving points of dispute). Each transition calculates the next deadline from the trigger date using the applicable CPR timeline. The client portal uses a completely separate session context from firm authentication — no shared session state — to prevent privilege escalation.

Key lessons: RLS-first architecture makes security testable independently of the application; CPR procedural modelling required a costs lawyer reviewer at design stage; client and firm authentication must be completely separated; audit trail design is an architectural decision, not a feature; beta partners surface edge cases no internal testing anticipates.

---

### AI Integration vs. AI-Native Software: What's the Right Approach?

Published: 2026-01-13 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/ai-integration-vs-ai-native-software

AI integration means adding AI capabilities to an existing software product — the existing system remains the primary architecture, AI is a capability layer. AI-native software is built with AI as a core architectural component from the ground up — data model, UX, and processing logic are all designed around AI capabilities, not adapted to accommodate them.

Choose integration when: the existing system accommodates AI without significant restructuring; the use case is well-defined and bounded; the existing data model already captures AI inputs; the integration can be a stateless function; speed to market is the priority. Choose AI-native when: AI capability is the primary value proposition; the existing data model does not support AI inputs (no provision for embeddings or conversation history); AI must be embedded in every layer of the UX; significant technical debt makes safe modification difficult; or starting from scratch.

Cost comparison: AI integration into a well-architected existing system can be delivered in 4–10 weeks. AI-native development follows full product development timelines — 4–9 months for a mid-complexity product. Integration is cheaper upfront; native is cheaper over five years if AI is genuinely core to the product. Two Bit Digital has delivered both approaches across legal tech, event technology, and enterprise systems.

---

### RegTech and Compliance Software: Why Regulated Industries Cannot Afford Generic Tools

Published: 2026-01-06 | Category: RegTech
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/regtech-compliance-software-regulated-industries

RegTech (Regulatory Technology) is software designed to help organisations manage regulatory compliance requirements. The defining characteristic of genuine RegTech: compliance requirements are embedded in the architecture, not added as a feature after the core product is built.

Why regulated industries need specialist software: audit requirements (tamper-evident logs of specific actions at granularity generic software does not provide), access control granularity (per-client or per-matter controls that standard tools cannot enforce), data residency and sovereignty requirements, mandatory encryption standards (AES-256 at rest, TLS in transit with verifiable key management), specific regulatory report formats, and defined liability architecture for data breaches.

Compliance-first architecture elements: audit trail at database level in an append-only table that cannot be modified through the application layer; row-level security enforced by the database itself; AES-256 encryption with key management that does not give the vendor access to client data; signed data processing agreements meeting GDPR and sector-specific requirements; automated data retention and deletion policies; regular third-party security assessment.

Zero-knowledge encryption means the software vendor has no access to the content of client data — only the client holds encryption keys. Even in a vendor infrastructure breach, client data remains encrypted and unreadable. Averon Legal Systems implements CPR compliance as architecture; Terra Core implements zero-knowledge document intelligence.

---

### How to Choose a SaaS Development Agency in the UK

Published: 2026-04-10 | Category: SaaS Development
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/how-to-choose-saas-development-agency-uk

Most SaaS builds fail not because of bad code, but because the agency never understood the product. Key checklist: Do they own a product themselves? Can they explain architecture decisions (not just outcomes)? Do they understand your regulatory context (GDPR, FCA, SRA, CQC)? Who specifically will work on your project day-to-day? Does the contract assign full IP ownership to you? What does post-launch support look like? Do they have case studies from your industry? Can you speak to a previous client directly?

Two Bit Digital operates three in-house products and applies real-world product experience to every client engagement.

---

### AI Integration for Regulated Industries: What Engineering Teams Get Wrong

Published: 2026-04-08 | Category: AI Engineering
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/ai-integration-regulated-industries

Key failures in regulated AI integration: AI outputs are not auditable by default — the same input can produce different outputs on different runs, with no native audit log. Every prompt and response must be logged with request IDs, timestamps, model version, and temperature settings. Data residency: default API tier terms from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are not sufficient for regulated use cases — enterprise DPAs specifying data residency and retention periods are required before processing personal data through any LLM API. Hallucination in high-stakes contexts (legal document review, compliance screening, clinical summarisation) creates professional liability — every AI output must be presented as a draft requiring human confirmation, not a decision requiring human override. RAG is the standard architecture for regulated AI — it retrieves specific identifiable documents, grounds model responses in them, and allows citation of sources.

### How Technology Companies Can Win UK Government Digital Contracts

Published: 2026-04-05 | Category: Government Digital
URL: https://twobitdigital.com/insights/winning-uk-government-digital-contracts

Three main routes to UK government technology contracts: G-Cloud (cloud catalogue allowing direct purchase by buyers without a full tender), DOS/Digital Outcomes and Specialists (specific project delivery with scored evaluation criteria), and Crown Commercial Service TPS. What procurement evaluators actually look for: specific evidence of similar work (sector, scale, outcome — not technology stack), demonstrated understanding of GDS standards and WCAG, named individuals with verifiable credentials, robust risk approach, social value commitments, and clear data and security articulation (Cyber Essentials, ISO 27001).

Two Bit Digital is eligible to respond to UK government procurement frameworks: Companies House 14710072, UN Vendor 1177996, D&B D-U-N-S 77-532-7428.

Q: What is Tikkit X?
A: Tikkit X is a mobile-first event ticketing and management platform built by Two Bit Digital for the Pakistani market. It features offline-capable HMAC-SHA256 cryptographic QR verification, native JazzCash and EasyPaisa payment integration, and a freemium pricing model. Events go live in under two minutes with no app download required for guests. Live at tikkitx.com.

Q: What is Averon Legal Systems?
A: Averon Legal Systems is a CPR Part 47 and Part 36 compliance SaaS built by Two Bit Digital for UK costs lawyers. It provides a matter lifecycle engine synchronised with CPR procedural deadlines, automated alerting, role-based dashboards for partners, supervisors and fee earners, structured document management, and a client portal. Currently in closed beta.

Q: Does Two Bit Digital build legal technology?
A: Yes. Two Bit Digital builds end-to-end digital solutions for law firms including client-facing websites, client portals with case diary access, secure document sharing, consultation booking, and complete internal management systems covering matter tracking, CPR deadline management, document management, case file digitisation, employee management, and audit trails. YKC Legal (ykclegal.org) is a live example of a law firm built out by Two Bit Digital.

Q: What is a RAG system?
A: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is an AI architecture that combines a document retrieval system with a language model. Documents are converted into embeddings stored in a vector database. When a question is asked, semantically similar documents are retrieved and passed to the language model alongside the question. The model generates a response grounded in those specific documents rather than general training data. This makes responses accurate, citable, and compliant with regulated industry auditability requirements.

Q: What is an AI workflow?
A: An AI workflow is a sequence of automated steps in which one or more AI models process, analyse, or generate content as part of a business process. Unlike traditional rule-based automation, AI workflows handle unstructured inputs like documents, emails, and natural language. Types include document processing, decision routing, conversational agents, data transformation, compliance monitoring, and content generation.

Q: What is RegTech?
A: RegTech (Regulatory Technology) is software designed to help organisations manage regulatory compliance requirements. Genuine RegTech embeds compliance requirements into the architecture from the ground up — including database-level audit trails, row-level security, AES-256 encryption with client-controlled keys, and data processing agreements. Two Bit Digital builds RegTech for legal, financial, and government sectors.
